exercise.name: Barbell Standing Back Wrist Curl
aliases: Standing palms-up barbell behind-the-back wrist curl

reference.title: Barbell Standing Back Wrist Curl
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the hands curl, inhale as they lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 1.7 s down

prescription.load: Bar load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control through the full range for every rep with 1-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-9).
prescription.progression: More reps, then a heavier bar

cues.text: Stand tall, feet hip width; hold the bar behind the thighs, palms facing back, hands about shoulder width, arms straight.
Breathe out and curl the bar up and back, bending only at the wrists.
Squeeze; the arms stay straight and still.
Breathe in and lower slowly until the hands hang straight.
Shoulders back and down, chest up; repeat.

mistakes.fix: Arms straight, shoulders down; only the wrists move.
Stand tall; the bar hangs just behind the thighs.

mistakes.mistake: Bar rubbing up the backs of the legs
mistakes.fix: Keep the arms a little behind the body.

kinematics.norm: Healthy adults used up to about 54 degrees of wrist flexion and 60 degrees of extension in daily tasks, functional range about 40 each way (Ryu 1991); a curl goes a little further, to a comfortable end range without pain (clinical opinion)
Arms straight, hanging just behind the thighs, still throughout (clinical opinion)
The bar stays just clear of the backs of the thighs and the buttocks (clinical opinion)

Slow and controlled, about 1 s up, a short squeeze and 1.5-2 s down (clinical opinion); resistance programmes for the wrist extensors in tendinopathy used 1-4 sets of about 15 reps, with no optimal dose defined (J Hand Ther 2012)

sources.title: GymVisual #4366, Barbell Standing Back Wrist Curl, video (movement reference)
Ryu, Cooney, Askew, An and Chao 1991, functional ranges of motion of the wrist joint (J Hand Surg Am 16(3):409-419; 40 adults, biaxial wrist electrogoniometer)
Szymanski, Szymanski, Molloy and Pascoe 2004, effect of 12 weeks of wrist and forearm training on high school baseball players (J Strength Cond Res 18(3):432-440; PubMed 15320673; 43 players)
Effectiveness of different methods of resistance exercises in lateral epicondylosis, a systematic review (J Hand Ther 2012;25(1):5-25; PubMed 22075055; 12 studies)

cautions: Front-of-shoulder discomfort with the arms behind the body: take a slightly wider grip or switch to the seated wrist curl (clinical opinion).
Wrist pain: lighter bar, smaller range (clinical opinion).
Take the bar from a rack set at hip height, or have a partner hand it over; do not swing it around behind you.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Dumbbells behind the back, one arm at a time.
Seated wrist curl if the shoulders do not like the behind-the-back position.
regressions: Empty bar or a light fixed barbell.

muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Curl the hands up and back behind the body; the finger flexors hold the bar. Added wrist and forearm work gave greater wrist and forearm strength gains (Szymanski 2004).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Curl the hands up and back behind the body; the finger flexors hold the bar. Added wrist and forearm work gave greater wrist and forearm strength gains (Szymanski 2004).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Holds the arms slightly behind the body so the bar clears the legs (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Holds the arms slightly behind the body so the bar clears the legs (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Draw the shoulders back so the arms can hang behind the thighs (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Draw the shoulders back so the arms can hang behind the thighs (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Carry the bar on the shoulders (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Carry the bar on the shoulders (clinical opinion).

phases.label: Arms straight, bar behind the thighs
Curl the hands up and back
